title: The Number Memorized That Day
description:
Months have passed. {name} scraped together seed money by sheer will.
And — that number memorized in the café that day,
Manager Kim 010-XXXX, still won't leave the mind.

3 AM. {name} picks up the phone. Puts it down.
That entry pass — could it still be live? One call would tell.

choices.result_text: It rang three times. My heart pounded along with it.

choices.text: Delete the number. Don't want to start with something stolen.
choices.result_text:
{name} deleted it. Fingers trembled slightly.
Another easy path discarded. But — somewhere deep in the mind,
a corner that had quietly turned dirty in that café finally felt clean again.
He wanted to start with both feet on his own ground.

title: The Call
description:
Three rings. "Hello."
Manager Kim doesn't remember {name}. {name} improvises.
"From the café that day... I was referred about the entry pass."

A brief silence. Then the voice softens.
"Ah, right. One slot still left. But the premium went up.
70 million won now. You need to decide today or tomorrow. So — you in?"

choices.text: Check first — verify the registry and market rate.
choices.result_text: {name} called two licensed brokers and cross-checked the figures.

choices.text: Trust the gut. Go all in. Everything.
choices.result_text: {name} hit transfer mid-call. Sometimes a gut feeling is the only evidence you get.

{name} quietly ended the call.
Too fast. "Today or tomorrow" kept nagging.
Hard sells always have a reason. Instinct said so.
Might have missed an opportunity. Might have dodged a trap. No way to know.

title: Digging In
description:
{name} spent three days on it. Registry, real estate forums, news.
The truth was half real — redevelopment confirmed. That part checked out.
But Manager Kim wasn't a co-op member or anything. Just a broker.
And 20 million won of that 70 million won was inflated foam — his "service fee."

A real opportunity wearing a fake price tag.

choices.result_text: {name} held the registry out to Manager Kim. "Twenty million of this is just foam." He looked away.

choices.text: Too risky like this. Walk away.
choices.result_text:
{name} pulled out. Manager Kim swore and hung up.
Later heard — the people who went in on that entry pass
got caught in the broker's markup and suffered for a long time after.
Those three days of digging saved {name}.

title: All In
description:
{name} emptied the account. No verification. No hesitation.
The number stolen in that café, the desire stolen in that café —
they finally pulled {name} all the way here.

The die is cast. If the redevelopment is real, life changes.
If not — back to zero.

choices.result_text: The account balance swung wildly. {name} stared at it for a long time.

title: Cutting the Foam
description:
{name} put the registry in front of Manager Kim.
"20 million won is foam. Let's do 50 million won. Otherwise I report it."
Manager Kim's face twisted. Then, reluctantly, a nod.
"...You can read a deal. Fine. 50 million won."

Only those who verify can negotiate. {name} got in at the right price.

choices.result_text: Risk still exists. But this time, it's a risk entered knowingly.

title: An Incoming Call
description:
Unknown number. The voice is familiar.
"Remember me? I caught you peeking through my folder at that café."
It was the man from that day. The one {name} received a card from with both hands.

"Wondering if you've done your homework. Small deal in circulation —
I only give it to people who are genuinely prepared. Interested?"

choices.result_text: They named a date and a place. {name} noted it down at once.

choices.text: "Not yet. I'll study more and get back to you."
choices.result_text:
The man was quiet a moment, then laughed.
"...Someone who can say that always comes eventually. Okay, take your time."
He hung up. The opportunity was deferred, but the door stayed open.
If anything — knowing how to say 'not yet' made him trust {name} more.

title: Verified Opportunity
description:
On the appointed day, back at the cafe, what the man put forward was clean. No foam, no manufactured urgency.
"A deal I'm watching personally. Not a jackpot, but it won't crack.
Come in within your means. Don't overextend."

Not stolen information — an opportunity vouched for by a person.
How different that is — {name} now knows.

choices.result_text: Not a big bet. But a solid first step.

choices.text: Still too much of a stretch. Wait for the next one.
choices.result_text:
"Not pushing is also a skill." The man nodded.
{name} let it go this time. But the relationship stayed.
Keeping a person is longer-lasting than any single opportunity.

title: Back at That Café
description:
{name} never forgot the humiliation.
'Learn before you try to run a scam.' Those words became fuel —
months of obsessive grinding through real estate. LTV, gaps — knows it all now.

Then by chance — same café, same man.
He recognizes {name}. "Hey, isn't that the bluffer?"

choices.text: Ask properly this time. With what was learned.
choices.result_text:
{name} spoke clearly. Right terms. Straight to the point.
The man's expression shifted. The smirk became curiosity.
"...You actually studied. That embarrassment taught you something."
For the first time, he treated {name} like a person.
Humiliation had been the sharpest teacher.

choices.text: Still too embarrassed. Head down, walk away.
choices.result_text:
{name} avoided his eyes and left the café.
The studying was done — but that day's shame still lived somewhere inside.
Someday — there'd be a day to face him head-on.
